goal: The century as a bar race: the ten largest cities trading places decade by decade, the source on screen, thirty seconds.
audience: anyone who likes watching a century move
assumptions: 16:9 (the request names no format; a chart race is landscape)
'the last century' = 1925-2025, a decade per beat
the data: each decade's top-ten by population, every figure a sourced fact (open data, snapshotted, the quote found in it)
the chart technique (the grown capability) — its data/axis gates are the piece's own quality bar

decision.why: The piece IS an animated data chart: the grown chart technique (motion-based, chart.json data, the data-gate requiring rows + a source and the axis-gate requiring numeric pairs) is the honest fit — a generic motion film would re-derive the same gates by hand.

alternatives.rejected_because: the same drawing without the chart gates: nothing would check the data file or the source — the grown technique's gates ARE the craft here

alternatives.id: simplest: a static table of today's top ten
alternatives.rejected_because: the simplest thing that could work — but 'over the last century' is the ask: the movement IS the meaning

segments.brief: Ten bars racing rank-by-rank, a decade per beat (1925-2025), the leader changes called by year labels, the source credited on screen throughout.
acceptance: every population figure on screen has a facts entry (snapshot + quote)
the pace: a decade per beat

risks: the dataset must be open and per-decade complete — a gap decade is hedged on screen, never invented
